project.name: Multivariate Polynomials
project.description: Reusable multivariate-polynomial results on infinite-variable ideals, coordinate-difference evaluation ideals, polynomial maximal-spectrum infinitude and the classification of univariate polynomial closed points by algebraic-closure automorphism orbits without separability, normal-extension automorphism orbits as minimal-polynomial root sets with cardinality equal to separable degree and full degree exactly for separable elements, homogeneous evaluation, disjoint-block substitution and its iteration, finite-variable origins of finite collections of polynomial fractions over integral domains in arbitrary fraction-ring representations, and a Krull-dimension bound for subsemirings by their finite-variable fraction-stage preimage dimensions, not the whole stage fields, degree, coefficient extraction and linear evaluation, chosen linear division, existential monic lifts and scalar-top first-variable lex degree. The univariate Hilbert basis theorem holds for any left-Noetherian ring, without coefficient commutativity, using a central variable and the canonical left self-module. The same holds for finitely many central natural-number coordinates via AddMonoidAlgebra, with independent coefficient and coordinate universes. Central Laurent polynomial rings over left-Noetherian rings are likewise left-Noetherian, including noncommutative and zero coefficient rings. The Laurent argument clears negative exponents by units and reuses the arbitrary-ring polynomial theorem. A polynomial point quotient by indexed squares and linear point relations has a canonical map to a square-zero extension of evaluation quotients; that same map is an algebra equivalence under pairwise unit differences. See README.md and docs/API.md for precise hypotheses and limitations.

headlines.title: Heights of homogeneous polynomial evaluations
headlines.text:
**Heights of homogeneous polynomial evaluations.** Over any field with
`Height.AdmissibleAbsValues`, a homogeneous polynomial family of common degree
`d`, with finite input and output coordinate types and no nonzero common zero
over an algebraic closure, has evaluation height uniformly comparable to the
input height raised to `d`. More precisely,
[`Height.exists_logHeight_eval_sub_mul_bound`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/Height/Homogeneous.lean)
bounds the difference between evaluation logarithmic height and `d` times input
logarithmic height, while
[`Height.exists_mulHeight_eval_bounds`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/Height/Homogeneous.lean)
bounds positive multiplicative height above and below by reciprocal constant
factors, with comparison constant at least one. The coordinate universes are
independent. Zero tuples, degree zero and empty coordinate types are included.

headlines.title: Homogeneous polynomial maps on projective coordinate spaces
headlines.text:
**Homogeneous polynomial maps on projective coordinate spaces.**
[`MvPolynomial.projectivize`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/Projectivization.lean)
sends a nonzero tuple's class to the class of its polynomial evaluation tuple.
The coefficients may lie in any commutative semiring equipped with a homomorphism
to the field of points. A common homogeneity degree and nonvanishing on nonzero
input tuples make this map well-defined; its values on these classes characterize
it uniquely. Coordinate variables induce the identity, and homogeneous
substitution induces composition. The coordinate types may be infinite or empty,
their universes are independent, and the degree may be zero. With coefficients
in the field of points, finite coordinates and admissible absolute values, the
[projective height comparisons](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/Height/Projectivization.lean)
descend the tuple bounds under the same algebraic-closure common-zero condition.

headlines.title: Homogeneous coordinate-power certificates
headlines.text:
**Homogeneous coordinate-power certificates.**
For an arbitrarily indexed homogeneous family `p : J → MvPolynomial I R`
of common degree `d` over any commutative semiring, with finitely many
variables, the
[certificate module](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/HomogeneousCertificates.lean)
states that radical membership of every variable gives finitely supported
coefficients `q : I → (J →₀ MvPolynomial I R)` and one common `M`, with
every `q i j` homogeneous of degree `M` and
`(q i).sum (fun j r => r * p j) = X i ^ (M + d)`. Over a field, the second
statement replaces radical membership by absence of nonzero common zeros
over the algebraic closure. The finite-index function-sum corollaries
`exists_homogeneous_sum_mul_eq_X_pow` and
`exists_homogeneous_sum_mul_eq_X_pow_of_forall_aeval_eq_zero` convert these
conclusions to `∑ j, q (i, j) * p j = X i ^ (M + d)` using
`Finsupp.sum_fintype`.
The variable, generator and coefficient universes are independent; empty
types, trivial semirings and degree zero are included. The
[coordinate-power and constant-one examples](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomialsTests/HomogeneousCertificates.lean)
verify the hypotheses and explicit certificates independently of the core statements.

headlines.title: Polynomial closed points and algebraic-closure orbits
headlines.text:
**Polynomial closed points and algebraic-closure orbits.** For independently
universed fields `K` and `L` with their given `Algebra K L` and
`IsAlgClosure K L`,
[`Polynomial.algAutOrbitEquivMaximalSpectrum`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/PolynomialClosedPoints.lean)
identifies the existing quotient of `L` by its `K`-algebra automorphism orbits
with `MaximalSpectrum K[X]`. The ideal of the orbit of `a` is the kernel of
`aeval a`, equivalently the ideal generated by `minpoly K a`. No perfectness
or separability is assumed. This is a set equivalence; over an imperfect
field, a singleton orbit need not be a rational point.

headlines.title: Infinitely many maximal ideals of polynomial rings
headlines.text:
**Infinitely many maximal ideals of polynomial rings.** Every nontrivial
commutative ring `R` has infinitely many maximal ideals in `R[X]`, including
when `R` is a finite field, by
[`MaximalSpectrum.infinite_polynomial`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/PrimeSpectrum.lean).
For any commutative ring `R` and arbitrary variable type `σ`, the maximal
spectrum of `MvPolynomial σ R` is infinite exactly when `R` is nontrivial
and either `σ` is nonempty or the maximal spectrum of `R` is infinite, by
[`MaximalSpectrum.infinite_mvPolynomial_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/PrimeSpectrum.lean).

headlines.title: Factorization uniqueness from a regular crossed resultant
headlines.text:
**Factorization uniqueness from a regular crossed resultant.** Over any commutative
ring, let `G,G'` have degree at most `m` and `H,H'` degree at most `n`, with
`G.coeff m = G'.coeff m` and `H.coeff n = H'.coeff n`. If `G * H = G' * H'`
and `Polynomial.resultant G' H m n` is regular, then `G = G'` and `H = H'`, by
[`Polynomial.eq_and_eq_of_mul_eq_mul_of_isRegular_resultant`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/ResultantFactorization.lean).
Neither monicity nor positive nominal degrees are required, and the ring may have
zero divisors.

headlines.title: Non-unital rings of additive units
headlines.text:
**Non-unital rings of additive units.** For a non-unital, non-associative semiring
`R`, the existing `AddUnits R` inherits multiplication and forms a non-unital,
non-associative ring. Associativity and commutativity are inherited when present.
For every non-unital, non-associative ring `S`, value inclusion induces
`(S →ₙ+* AddUnits R) ≃ (S →ₙ+* R)`, with a unique factorization through the
additive units. See [`AddUnits`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/AddUnits.lean).

headlines.title: Nonconstant coefficients of polynomial units
headlines.text:
**Nonconstant coefficients of polynomial units.** Over any commutative semiring
`R`, every coefficient at a nonzero exponent of a unit in `MvPolynomial σ R`
is additively invertible, by
[`MvPolynomial.isAddUnit_coeff_of_isUnit`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/UnitCoefficients.lean).
The variable type is arbitrary, including empty and infinite types.

headlines.title: Polynomial units over commutative semirings
headlines.text:
**Polynomial units over commutative semirings.** For any commutative semiring
`R` and arbitrary variable type `σ`, a polynomial in `MvPolynomial σ R` is a
unit if and only if its constant coefficient is a unit and its coefficient at
every nonzero exponent is both nilpotent and additively invertible, by
[`MvPolynomial.isUnit_iff_coeff_isNilpotent_isAddUnit`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/UnitCriterion.lean).
The coefficient and variable types have independent universes; empty variable
types and the zero semiring are included. The lemma
[`MvPolynomial.isUnit_coeff_zero_and_isNilpotent_isAddUnit_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/UnitCriterion.lean)
identifies the coefficient conditions over a commutative ring with those in
Mathlib's `MvPolynomial.isUnit_iff`. The sufficiency direction remains available as
[`MvPolynomial.isUnit_of_coeff_isNilpotent_isAddUnit`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/UnitSufficiency.lean).

headlines.title: Prime coefficient extensions over commutative semirings
headlines.text:
**Prime coefficient extensions over commutative semirings.** For a commutative
semiring `R`, any variable type `σ` and ideal `I`, primality of `I` together
with `∀ a b : R, a ∈ I → a + b ∈ I → b ∈ I` implies primality of
`I.map MvPolynomial.C`,
by [`MvPolynomial.isPrime_map_C_of_subtractive`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/CoefficientIdealPrime.lean).
For nonempty `σ`, these conditions are also necessary, by
[`MvPolynomial.isPrime_map_C_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/CoefficientIdealPrime.lean).

headlines.title: Maximal coefficient extensions over commutative semirings
headlines.text:
**Maximal coefficient extensions over commutative semirings.** For a commutative
semiring `R`, any variable type `σ` and ideal `I`,
`(I.map MvPolynomial.C).IsMaximal ↔ I.IsMaximal ∧ IsEmpty σ`, by
[`MvPolynomial.isMaximal_map_C_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/CoefficientIdealMaximal.lean).
With nonempty `σ`, no coefficient extension is maximal. For proper `I`,
the constant-coefficient preimage is a strict intermediate ideal.

headlines.title: Finite coefficient-product equations determine whole products
headlines.text:
**Finite coefficient-product equations determine whole products.** For independent
commutative semirings `C` and `R`, an arbitrary homomorphism `φ : C →+* R`,
nominal sizes `m,n`, seeds `g,h : Polynomial C` and arbitrary target coefficient
point, [`MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom_coefficientProduct_eq_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/CoefficientProduct.lean)
identifies the finite evaluated equations with equality of the entire ordinary
perturbed product to `T`. It assumes target-side bounds
`(g.map φ).natDegree ≤ m`, `(h.map φ).natDegree ≤ n`, `T.natDegree ≤ m + n`, and
`T.coeff (m + n) = (g.map φ).coeff m * (h.map φ).coeff n`. Zero sizes, mapped
degree drops and trivial semirings are included; no source degree bound or
injectivity of `φ` is required.

headlines.title: Radicals of coefficient-ideal extensions
headlines.text:
**Radicals of coefficient-ideal extensions.** For any commutative ring `R`,
arbitrary variable type `σ` and ideal `I : Ideal R`,
[`MvPolynomial.radical_map_C`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/IdealExtension.lean)
says that extending `I` along the constant-polynomial map commutes with radicals.
[`MvPolynomial.mem_radical_map_C_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/IdealExtension.lean)
characterizes radical membership coefficientwise: a polynomial lies in the
radical of the extended ideal exactly when every coefficient lies in `I.radical`.

headlines.title: Scalar annihilators and non-zero-divisors
headlines.text:
**Scalar annihilators and non-zero-divisors.** For any commutative semiring
`R` and arbitrary variable type `σ`,
[`MvPolynomial.mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/Regularity.lean)
characterizes non-zero-divisors by the absence of a nonzero scalar in the
original coefficient semiring annihilating every coefficient. No individual
coefficient need be a non-zero-divisor.
[`MvPolynomial.eq_zero_of_mul_eq_zero_of_smul`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/Regularity.lean)
shows that a polynomial with no nonzero scalar annihilator has no nonzero
polynomial annihilator. The results allow empty or infinite variable types,
independent universes and trivial coefficient semirings. The interpretation
in terms of `IsRegular` is asserted only over commutative rings.

headlines.title: The degree-zero homogeneous component
headlines.text:
**The degree-zero homogeneous component.** For any commutative semiring
`R` and arbitrary variable type `σ`,
[`MvPolynomial.gradeZeroAlgEquiv`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/GradeZero.lean)
identifies `R` as an `R`-algebra with Mathlib's original degree-zero homogeneous
component. Its forward map is the inherited coefficient algebra map, with
ambient polynomial `C r`; its inverse is `constantCoeff`. The construction uses
independent universes and commutes with coefficient homomorphisms in the
ambient polynomial algebras, without finiteness or nontriviality hypotheses.

headlines.title: Coefficient ideals over commutative semirings
headlines.text:
**Coefficient ideals over commutative semirings.** For any commutative
semiring `R`, ideal `I` and arbitrary variable type `σ`,
[`MvPolynomial.coeffsIn_eq_restrictScalars_map_C`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/CoefficientIdeal.lean)
identifies the extension `Ideal.map C I`, restricted to the canonical
coefficient action, with Mathlib's coefficient submodule `coeffsIn σ I`.
Polynomial membership is therefore coefficientwise membership, and
contraction along `C` recovers `I`.
[`MvPolynomial.ker_map_eq_map_C`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/CoefficientIdeal.lean)
identifies the kernel of a coefficient map with the extension of its kernel.
Coefficients, target coefficients and variables have independent universes;
no ring, finiteness or nontriviality hypothesis is needed. The
[natural-number example](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomialsTests/CoefficientIdeal.lean)
separates `2 * X` from `X` for the proper extended ideal `(2)` and for
coefficient reduction modulo two.

headlines.title: Square witnesses for failure of subtractivity
headlines.text:
**Square witnesses for failure of subtractivity.** Over any commutative
semiring `R`, for `i : σ` and `a b : R`,
[`MvPolynomial.subtractiveWitness`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/CoefficientIdealSubtractive.lean)
is `C a + C b * X i + C (a + b) * X i ^ 2`, with linear coefficient `b`.
Its square belongs to `I.map C` if `a ∈ I` and `a + b ∈ I`, while
`b ∉ I` excludes the witness itself. Thus a radical (in particular prime)
extension over nonempty variables forces subtractivity. Coefficient and
variable universes are independent; no finiteness or nontriviality is needed.

headlines.title: Powers of augmented coefficient ideals
headlines.text:
**Powers of augmented coefficient ideals.** For any commutative semiring
`R`, ideal `I`, natural number `n`, arbitrary variable type `σ`, and polynomial
`p`, [`MvPolynomial.mem_pow_comap_constantCoeff_iff_coeff_mem_pow`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/AugmentedIdealPowers.lean)
characterizes membership in `(I.comap constantCoeff) ^ n`: the coefficient
at each exponent `d` belongs to `I ^ (n - d.sum (fun _ k => k))`.
Subtraction is truncated in `ℕ`, so degrees at least `n` impose no
restriction, rather than vanishing. Coefficients and variables have
independent universes; empty or infinite variables and trivial coefficient
semirings are allowed. The bottom coefficient ideal recovers Mathlib's
variable-ideal power criterion. The
[integer and boundary examples](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomialsTests/CoefficientVariableIdeal.lean)
apply the criterion to `2 * X ∈ (2, X)²`, contrast the constant `2`, and
include the zeroth power and empty variables.

headlines.title: Primary coefficient ideals
headlines.text:
**Primary coefficient ideals.** Over any commutative semiring `R`,
[`MvPolynomial.isPrimary_map_C_of_subtractive`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/Primary.lean)
extends a primary ideal `I` satisfying `a ∈ I → a + b ∈ I → b ∈ I` to a
primary coefficient ideal, for every variable type `σ`. When `σ` is nonempty,
[`MvPolynomial.isPrimary_map_C_iff_subtractive`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/Primary.lean)
proves that primaryness and this subtractivity condition are also necessary.
For a commutative ring, subtractivity is automatic, and
[`MvPolynomial.isPrimary_map_C_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/Primary.lean)
gives the equivalence without any restriction on `σ`. Coefficients and
variables have independent universes; empty variable types and the unit ideal
are included, with no Noetherian or nontriviality hypothesis. The
[integer example](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomialsTests/Primary.lean) extends the
primary, nonradical ideal `(4)`.

headlines.title: Supplied primary families and deletion irredundance
headlines.text:
**Supplied primary families and deletion irredundance.** Over a commutative
semiring `R`, for an ideal `I` and family `Q : ι → Ideal R`,
[`MvPolynomial.primary_family_map_C_iff_of_subtractive`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/PrimaryDecomposition.lean)
assumes `a ∈ Q i → a + b ∈ Q i → b ∈ Q i` for each component. For every variable
type `σ`, it equates `I.map C = ⨅ i, (Q i).map C` with all mapped components
primary to `I = ⨅ i, Q i` with all original components primary. For nonempty
`σ`, [`MvPolynomial.primary_family_map_C_iff_subtractive`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/PrimaryDecomposition.lean)
gives the exact equivalence with `I = ⨅ i, Q i` and componentwise primaryness
and subtractivity, recovering the latter from the mapped primary family.
The ring theorem
[`MvPolynomial.primary_family_map_C_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/PrimaryDecomposition.lean)
specializes the first equivalence using automatic subtractivity, for every `σ`.
The intersection itself need not be primary. Over any commutative semiring,
[`MvPolynomial.irredundant_iInf_map_C_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/PrimaryDecomposition.lean)
preserves and reflects the condition that each intersection of the other
components is not contained in the omitted component, without subtractivity.
Indices may form any sort; coefficient, variable and index universes are
independent. Empty or infinite families are allowed, with no finiteness or
Noetherian hypothesis. These statements give no existence, uniqueness or
associated-prime claim. The
[integer model](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomialsTests/PrimaryDecomposition.lean)
uses the ring equivalence and deletion irredundance for `(12) = (4) ∩ (3)`.

headlines.title: Nilpotent coefficients and irreducible polynomial spectra
headlines.text:
**Nilpotent coefficients and irreducible polynomial spectra.** For any
commutative semiring `R` and arbitrary variable type `σ`,
[`MvPolynomial.isNilpotent_iff_coeff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/Nilpotent.lean)
characterizes nilpotent polynomials by nilpotence of every coefficient.
[`PrimeSpectrum.irreducibleSpace_mvPolynomial_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/PrimeSpectrum.lean)
states that `PrimeSpectrum (MvPolynomial σ R)` is irreducible exactly when
`PrimeSpectrum R` is irreducible. Coefficients and variables have independent
universes; empty or infinite variables and trivial coefficients are allowed.

headlines.title: Jacobson radicals of coefficient ideals
headlines.text:
**Jacobson radicals of coefficient ideals.** For any commutative ring `R`,
ideal `I` and nonempty variable type `σ`,
[`Ideal.jacobson_map_mvPolynomial_C`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/Jacobson.lean)
identifies `Ideal.jacobson (I.map C)` with `I.radical.map C`.
In particular, the Jacobson radical of zero in `MvPolynomial σ R` is its
nilradical. Coefficient and variable universes are independent; no
Jacobson-ring, Noetherian, properness or nontriviality hypothesis is needed.
The [integer example](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomialsTests/Jacobson.lean) separates
the extended ideal `(4)` from its proper Jacobson radical using `2 * X`.

headlines.title: Integral elements over coefficient rings
headlines.text:
**Integral elements over coefficient rings.** For any commutative ring `R`
and arbitrary variable type `σ`,
[`MvPolynomial.isIntegral_iff_coeff_isNilpotent`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/IntegralCoefficients.lean)
characterizes `IsIntegral R p` by nilpotence of every nonconstant coefficient.
For reduced `R`,
[`MvPolynomial.isIntegral_iff_eq_C_coeff_zero`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/IntegralCoefficients.lean)
specializes this to `p = C (p.coeff 0)`.
The coefficient and variable universes are independent; trivial coefficient
rings and empty or infinite variable types are allowed. Over `ZMod 4`,
`C 2 * X ()` is a nonconstant square-zero integral polynomial.

headlines.title: Integral closure in arbitrarily many variables
headlines.text:
**Integral closure in arbitrarily many variables.** For every integrally closed
commutative domain `R` and arbitrary variable type `ι`,
[`MvPolynomial.isIntegrallyClosed`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/IntegrallyClosed.lean)
makes the ordinary polynomial ring `MvPolynomial ι R` integrally closed.
The coefficient and variable universes are independent, and the variables may
be empty or infinite. No Noetherian or unique-factorization hypothesis is
imposed on `R`.

headlines.title: Flatness of commutative-ring variable renaming
headlines.text:
**Flatness of commutative-ring variable renaming.** For every commutative
ring `R` and arbitrary `f : σ → τ`, with coefficient and variable types in
independent universes,
[`MvPolynomial.rename_flat_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/RenameFlatness.lean)
characterizes flatness of the full ring homomorphism
`MvPolynomial.rename (R := R) f` by injectivity of `f` or subsingleton
coefficients. The scalar action is induced by this original polynomial-ring
map, not just by `R` or by its image. Injective maps give free polynomial
extensions after complementary variables are separated; a collision kills
the regular difference of two distinct variables. The
[regularity API](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/Regularity.lean) works over every
commutative ring, including the zero ring. The
[independent models](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomialsTests/RenameFlatnessModels.lean)
and [criterion applications](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomialsTypeTests/RenameFlatness.lean)
include a proper inclusion over the integers, a collision over the nonreduced
ring `ZMod 4`, and the same collision over `ZMod 1`.
The same module also gives
[`MvPolynomial.comap_rename_surjective_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/RenameFlatness.lean)
for commutative semirings and
[`MvPolynomial.rename_faithfullyFlat_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/RenameFlatness.lean)
for commutative rings: each uses the same injectivity-or-subsingleton condition
for the original full polynomial map. Their criterion applications include
the strict inclusion over `ℤ`, prime-spectrum surjectivity over the non-ring
semiring `ℕ`, an empty source, and a collision over the zero ring.

headlines.title: Canonical unique-variable degree
headlines.text:
**Canonical unique-variable degree.** For any commutative semiring `R`,
unique variable type `σ` (`[Unique σ]`), and `p : MvPolynomial σ R`,
[`MvPolynomial.natDegree_uniqueAlgEquiv`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/UniqueAlgEquiv.lean)
identifies `Polynomial.natDegree (MvPolynomial.uniqueAlgEquiv R σ p)`
with `p.totalDegree`. The coefficient and variable universes are independent.
No nonzero-polynomial or nontrivial-coefficient premise is needed:
both natural-number degrees assign zero to the zero polynomial.

headlines.title: Injectivity and surjectivity of variable renaming
headlines.text:
**Injectivity and surjectivity of variable renaming.** For any commutative
semiring `R` and any map `f : σ → τ`, with the coefficient, source-variable
and target-variable types in independent universes, the canonical renaming
map from the full polynomial semiring `MvPolynomial σ R` to the full
polynomial semiring `MvPolynomial τ R` is injective exactly when `f` is
injective or `R` is subsingleton
([`MvPolynomial.injective_rename_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/Rename.lean)),
and is surjective exactly when `f` is surjective or `R` is subsingleton
([`MvPolynomial.surjective_rename_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/Rename.lean)).

headlines.title: Formal smoothness of variable renaming
headlines.text:
**Formal smoothness of variable renaming.** Over any commutative ring `R`,
[`MvPolynomial.rename_formallySmooth_iff_injective`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/RenameFormalSmoothness.lean)
characterizes formal smoothness of the full source polynomial-ring
homomorphism by injectivity of that homomorphism. Equivalently,
[`MvPolynomial.rename_formallySmooth_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/RenameFormalSmoothness.lean)
says that the variable map is injective or the coefficients are subsingleton.
The scalar action is induced by the original renaming, not just by `R`.
The coefficient and variable types have independent universes, with no
finiteness or nontriviality hypotheses. Complementary variables give the
polynomial-extension direction; a square-zero lifting obstruction detects
collisions over nontrivial coefficients.

headlines.title: Smoothness of variable renaming
headlines.text:
**Smoothness of variable renaming.** Over any commutative ring `R`,
[`MvPolynomial.rename_smooth_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/RenameSmooth.lean)
says that the canonical homomorphism on full polynomial rings is smooth
exactly when the variable map is injective with finite complement, or `R`
is subsingleton. This is stock `RingHom.Smooth`, including finite
presentation, for the source-polynomial action induced by renaming.
Coefficients and both variable types have independent universes; no
finiteness or nontriviality hypothesis is imposed on them.
[`MvPolynomial.rename_smooth_iff_flat_and_finiteType`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/RenameSmooth.lean)
compares smoothness with flatness and finite type for these renamings.
Five concrete settings in the same file distinguish the collision/flatness
obstruction from the infinite-complement/finite-type obstruction and exhibit
the zero-ring exception. A derived application uses the comparison to extract
flatness and finite type from an independent one-variable extension over `ℤ`.

headlines.title: Formal unramifiedness of variable renaming
headlines.text:
**Formal unramifiedness of variable renaming.** Over any commutative ring
`R`, [`MvPolynomial.formallyUnramified_rename_iff_surjective`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/RenameUnramified.lean)
says that `MvPolynomial.rename f`, as a homomorphism from the full source
polynomial ring, is formally unramified exactly when it is surjective:
equivalently, when `f` is surjective or `R` is subsingleton. The coefficient
and variable types may lie in independent universes, and neither variable
type must be finite or inhabited. The [private boundary models](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/RenameUnramified.lean)
include a collision of variables over the integers, an omitted variable over
the integers, and an omitted variable over `ZMod 1`. The collision uses
`MvPolynomial.formallyUnramified_rename_iff_moduleFinite`, with the full source
polynomial ring acting by multiplication by the renamed polynomial.

headlines.title: Integrality of polynomial variable renaming
headlines.text:
**Integrality of polynomial variable renaming.**
Over any commutative ring `R`,
[`MvPolynomial.isIntegral_rename_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/RenameIntegral.lean)
states that renaming between the full polynomial rings is integral exactly
when the variable map is surjective or the coefficient ring is subsingleton.
See the [integrality section](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/README.md#integrality-of-polynomial-variable-renaming)
for the precise map, generality and applications.

headlines.title: Algebraicity of polynomial variable renaming
headlines.text:
**Algebraicity of polynomial variable renaming.**
Over any commutative ring `R`,
[`MvPolynomial.isAlgebraic_rename_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/RenameAlgebraic.lean)
states that the full target polynomial ring is algebraic over the full source
via the specified renaming exactly when the coefficients are nontrivial and
the variable map is surjective or noninjective. A collision gives a nonzero
constant annihilator, even when a target variable is missed; zero coefficients
give no such polynomial, even for identity renaming. This is weak algebraicity,
not integrality or module finiteness. The coefficient and both variable types
have independent universes, with no additional ring or finiteness hypotheses.
[Criterion applications](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/RenameAlgebraic.lean)
are colocated with the public result. The independent
[positive models](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/RenameAlgebraic.lean)
and [negative models](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/RenameAlgebraic.lean)
use stock Mathlib directly for algebraicity. The shifted-projection models over
the integers and `ZMod 4` use the existing integrality criterion for their
missing-variable nonintegrality proofs:
[`MvPolynomial.isIntegral_X_rename_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/RenameIntegral.lean).

headlines.title: Finite presentation of commutative-ring variable renaming
headlines.text:
**Finite presentation of commutative-ring variable renaming.**
[`MvPolynomial.finitePresentation_rename_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/RenameFinitePresentation.lean)
states the relative finite-presentation criterion: subsingleton coefficients,
or finitely many missed target variables together with finitely many source
collision participants. Both collision endpoints are counted. See the
[finite-presentation section](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/README.md#relative-finite-presentation-of-variable-renaming)
for the coefficient-ring boundary and infinite-variable examples.

headlines.title: Zero-variable presentations and semiring renaming
headlines.text:
**Zero-variable presentations and semiring renaming.**
[`Algebra.FinitePresentation.of_surjective_algebraMap`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/FinitePresentation.lean)
gives a zero-variable presentation for a surjective scalar map from a
commutative semiring to any semiring, with finitely generated ideal kernel.
For commutative-semiring coefficients with subsingleton additive units,
[renaming reflects zero](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/RenameFinitePresentationSemiring.lean)
and every surjective variable map is finitely presented over its full source
polynomial semiring. No cancellation, order, or finiteness assumption is needed.
This is Mathlib's ideal-kernel convention, not congruence-based semiring
finite presentation; a bottom ideal kernel need not imply injectivity.

headlines.title: Variable renaming has an exact relative finite-type criterion
headlines.text:
**Variable renaming has an exact relative finite-type criterion.**
[`MvPolynomial.finiteType_rename_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/RenameFiniteType.lean)
characterizes finite generation of the target polynomial algebra over the
source polynomial semiring: the coefficients are subsingleton or the set of
missed target variables is finite. See the
[relative finite-type section](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/README.md#relative-finite-type-of-variable-renaming)
for the algebra structure, generality and infinite-variable applications.

headlines.title: Variable renaming has an exact relative essentially finite-type criterion
headlines.text:
**Variable renaming has an exact relative essentially finite-type criterion.**
[`MvPolynomial.essFiniteType_rename_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/RenameEssentialFiniteType.lean)
characterizes `RingHom.EssFiniteType` of renaming for arbitrary `f : σ → τ`
over a commutative ring `R`, with independent coefficient and variable
universes: `R` is subsingleton or `Set.Finite ((Set.range f)ᶜ)`. Scalars are
`MvPolynomial σ R`, acting on `MvPolynomial τ R` by `p • q = rename f p * q`.
Essential finite type is distinct from finite type, but their criteria
coincide for these maps. The
[worked applications](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/RenameEssentialFiniteType.lean)
contrast successor renaming over `ℤ` (only `0` is missed), `Empty → ℕ`
with subsingleton coefficients (infinitely many missed variables), and
even-index renaming over `ℤ`, which is not essentially of finite type.

headlines.title: Module finiteness of variable renaming has a sharper criterion
headlines.text:
**Module finiteness of variable renaming has a sharper criterion.** For any
commutative semiring `R` and any map `f : σ → τ`, with all three types in
independent universes,
[`MvPolynomial.moduleFinite_rename_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/RenameModuleFinite.lean)
states that the full target polynomial semiring is a finite module over the
full source polynomial semiring under `p • q = MvPolynomial.rename f p * q`
exactly when `f` is surjective or `R` is subsingleton. This is stronger than
finite type: over nontrivial coefficients, `Nat.succ : ℕ → ℕ` misses only
`0`, so its renaming is of finite type but is not module-finite. These are
source-polynomial scalars, not coefficient-`R` scalars. See the
[applications beside the criterion](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/RenameModuleFinite.lean),
including nonreduced and noncancellative coefficients and independent universe lifts.

headlines.title: Quasi-finiteness of commutative-ring variable renaming
headlines.text:
**Quasi-finiteness of commutative-ring variable renaming.** For any
commutative ring `R` and arbitrary `f : σ → τ`, with all three types in
independent universes,
[`MvPolynomial.rename_quasiFinite_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/RenameQuasiFinite.lean)
states that the original full polynomial-ring map is quasi-finite exactly
when `f` is surjective or `R` is subsingleton. It uses Mathlib's
residue-field-fiber convention, without a `FiniteType` hypothesis, and
the full source-polynomial action. Module finiteness supplies the positive
direction; an omitted target variable gives a surjective evaluation onto
`R[X]`, reducing the converse to Mathlib's polynomial local obstruction. The
comparison `MvPolynomial.rename_quasiFinite_iff_finite` identifies
quasi-finiteness with finiteness of that same ring homomorphism. The
[boundary applications](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/RenameQuasiFinite.lean)
contrast an omitted variable and a noninjective surjection over `ℤ`, and
include the same omitted-variable map over `ZMod 1`. In the collision case,
a nonzero source polynomial annihilates every target polynomial under the
full renaming-induced action.

headlines.title: Finite coefficient aggregation has an exact injectivity criterion
headlines.text:
**Finite coefficient aggregation has an exact injectivity criterion.** For
types `α`, `β` and `M` in independent universes, an additive commutative
monoid `M`, and any index map `f : α → β`,
[`Finsupp.mapDomain_injective_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/FiniteSupport.lean)
characterizes injectivity of `Finsupp.mapDomain f : (α →₀ M) → (β →₀ M)`:
it holds exactly when `f` is injective **or** `M` is subsingleton. The map
adds coefficients whose indices have the same image; cancellation, a ring
structure and nontrivial coefficients are not required. The
[applications](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomialsTests/FiniteSupport.lean) contrast the
identity and a constant index map with natural-number coefficients.

headlines.title: Joint degree-and-support profiles recover bivariate coefficients only for trivial coefficients
headlines.text:
**Joint degree-and-support profiles recover bivariate coefficients only for trivial coefficients.**
For any additive commutative monoid `M` in an arbitrary universe,
[`Finsupp.mapDomain_degree_support_hasLeftInverse_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/FiniteSupport.lean)
proves that pushing coefficients along
`d ↦ (d.degree, d.support.card)`, for `d : Fin 2 →₀ ℕ`, admits a total left
inverse exactly when `M` is subsingleton. The profile groups coefficients
jointly by total degree and the number of variables with positive exponent.
The decoder may be **any total function**: no additive, multiplicative or
linear structure is required. The
[applications](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomialsTests/FiniteSupport.lean) exclude every
decoder over `ℕ` and obtain recovery over the zero ring `ZMod 1`.

headlines.title: Variable-renaming kernels have an exact presentation and finite-generation criterion
headlines.text:
**Variable-renaming kernels have an exact presentation and finite-generation criterion.**
For any commutative ring `R` and any map `f : σ → τ`, with all three types in
independent universes,
[`MvPolynomial.ker_rename_eq_span_X_sub_X`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/RenameKernel.lean)
identifies the kernel of `MvPolynomial.rename (R := R) f` with the ideal
generated by `X i - X j` for pairs satisfying `f i = f j`. Moreover,
[`MvPolynomial.ker_rename_fg_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/RenameKernel.lean)
says that this ideal is finitely generated exactly when `R` is subsingleton
or the set `{i : σ | ∃ j : σ, i ≠ j ∧ f i = f j}` is finite. This counts
**both endpoints** of every collision, not just chosen representatives;
finiteness of individual fibres is not enough. Finite generation is as an
ideal of the **source polynomial ring** `MvPolynomial σ R`, not as an
`R`-module. No surjectivity or finite-variable hypothesis is required. See
the [applications](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomialsTests/RenameKernelCriterion.lean).

headlines.title: Fraction-ring renaming is surjective, equivalently integral, exactly when it covers all variables
headlines.text:
**Fraction-ring renaming is surjective, equivalently integral, exactly when
it covers all variables.**
For any integral domain `R` (`[CommRing R] [IsDomain R]`) and injective
`ρ : τ → σ`,
[`MvPolynomial.surjective_fractionRing_map_rename_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/FractionRingFiniteVariables.lean)
characterizes surjectivity of the induced fraction-ring map by
`Function.Surjective ρ`. Its source `L` and target `K` may be any
commutative-ring fraction-ring realizations with their `Algebra` and
`IsFractionRing` instances, without `Field` instances. The five universes
of `R`, `τ`, `σ`, `L` and `K` are independent. For this same map,
[`MvPolynomial.isIntegral_fractionRing_map_rename_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/FractionRingFiniteVariables.lean)
characterizes integrality by the same condition `Function.Surjective ρ`.
[`MvPolynomial.surjective_fractionRing_map_finset_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/FractionRingFiniteVariables.lean)
and
[`MvPolynomial.isIntegral_fractionRing_map_finset_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/FractionRingFiniteVariables.lean)
specialize these criteria to a finite-variable stage `S : Finset σ`: the
stage map is surjective, equivalently integral, exactly when
`∀ i : σ, i ∈ S`, with no finiteness hypothesis on the ambient variable
type. The variable-image criterion identifies the image of `X i` in the
range exactly when `i ∈ Set.range ρ`. When `i ∉ Set.range ρ`,
[`MvPolynomial.not_isIntegralElem_fractionRing_map_rename_X`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/FractionRingFiniteVariables.lean)
shows that the localized variable `X i` in `K` is not integral over the
image of the fraction-ring map. Thus every finite stage in infinitely
many variables is neither surjective nor integral, although each finite
family of fractions has a common finite stage. See the
[API guide](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/docs/API.md#multivariatepolynomialsfractionringfinitevariables).

headlines.title: Omitted variables are algebraically independent over the source fraction ring
headlines.text:
**Omitted variables are algebraically independent over the source fraction ring.**
For a commutative domain `R`, an injective map `ρ : τ → σ`, and arbitrary
commutative-ring fraction rings `L` of `MvPolynomial τ R` and `K` of
`MvPolynomial σ R`,
[`MvPolynomial.algebraicIndependent_fractionRing_map_rename_compl`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/FractionRingAlgebraicIndependence.lean)
proves that the images of `X i` in `K`, indexed by
`{i : σ // i ∉ Set.range ρ}`, are algebraically independent over `L`.
The `L`-algebra structure on `K` must be induced by the same canonical
fraction-ring map of `MvPolynomial.rename ρ`, not an arbitrary scalar action.
The five universes of `R`, `τ`, `σ`, `L` and `K` are independent;
no `Field` instances or finite index types are required.

headlines.title: Omitted variables form a transcendence basis over the source fraction ring
headlines.text:
**Omitted variables form a transcendence basis over the source fraction ring.**
In the same five-universe commutative-domain setting and under the full
canonical fraction-renaming scalar action,
[`MvPolynomial.isAlgebraic_adjoin_fractionRing_map_rename_compl`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/FractionRingTranscendenceBasis.lean)
proves that `K` is algebraic over the `L`-subalgebra generated by the
complementary localized variables, and
[`MvPolynomial.isTranscendenceBasis_fractionRing_map_rename_compl`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/FractionRingTranscendenceBasis.lean)
identifies that family as a transcendence basis over `L`. Under the same
hypotheses,
[`MvPolynomial.isFractionRing_adjoin_fractionRing_map_rename_compl`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/FractionRingTranscendenceBasis.lean)
makes `K` the fraction ring of that generated `L`-subalgebra, for its canonical
inclusion into `K`. The adjoin is over
the source **fraction ring**, not the coefficient ring. Neither fraction-ring
realization needs a `Field` instance, and neither variable type need be finite.
The [direct-import examples](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomialsTests/FractionRingTranscendenceBasis.lean)
include the nonempty complement of `Unit → Bool`, `() ↦ false`, over `ℤ`,
as well as arbitrary fraction-ring realizations.

headlines.title: Zeros are closed points of polynomial quotients
headlines.text:
**Zeros are closed points of polynomial quotients.** For any ideal `I` in
`MvPolynomial σ K` with `K` algebraically closed and `σ` finite, the
[canonical point-set equivalence](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/QuotientClosedPoints.lean)
identifies `MvPolynomial.zeroLocus K I` with closed points of the spectrum
of `MvPolynomial σ K ⧸ I`. The forward prime is the kernel of descended
evaluation; polynomial membership and inverse coordinates have explicit
laws. The field and variables may inhabit different universes, and `I` may
be the unit ideal or define a nonreduced quotient. This point-set result
itself does not assert a topological or sheaf equivalence.

headlines.title: The image of evaluating one polynomial at two points
headlines.text:
**The image of evaluating one polynomial at two points.**
Over any commutative ring `R`, for assignments `a b : σ → R` with independent
coefficient and variable universes,
[`MvPolynomial.mem_range_eval_prod_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/EvaluationIdeal.lean)
characterizes value pairs `(r, s) : R × R` of one common polynomial by
`r - s ∈ Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i => a i - b i))`, without a
finite-variable, field or comaximality assumption. The
[examples](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomialsTests/EvaluationIdealImage.lean)
contrast same-parity pairs at the one-variable integer points `0` and `2`
with all pairs at the two-variable points `(0, 0)` and `(2, 3)` despite
nonunit coordinate differences, and include empty-variable diagonal and
zero-ring boundaries.

headlines.title: Finite simultaneous polynomial evaluation has an exact surjectivity criterion
headlines.text:
**Finite simultaneous polynomial evaluation has an exact surjectivity criterion.**
For any commutative ring `R`, arbitrary variable type `σ`, finite point-index
type `ι` and family `a : ι → σ → R`,
[`MvPolynomial.surjective_eval_family_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/EvaluationIdeal.lean)
states that `p ↦ (i ↦ MvPolynomial.eval (a i) p)` is surjective exactly when
the coordinate differences `a i s - a j s`, for all `s : σ`, generate the
unit ideal for every pair of distinct indices `i ≠ j`. The three types have
independent universes. Empty families, empty or infinite variable types,
repeated points and the zero ring are included; no field hypothesis is needed.

headlines.title: Evaluation-kernel powers are detected by translated coefficients
headlines.text:
**Evaluation-kernel powers are detected by translated coefficients.** For any
commutative semiring `R` and point `a : σ → AddUnits R`,
[`MvPolynomial.mem_pow_ker_eval_addUnits_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/EvaluationIdeal.lean)
characterizes membership in every `n`th evaluation-kernel power by vanishing
of all coefficients of total degree `< n` after the translation `p(X + a)`.
Over a commutative ring,
[`MvPolynomial.mem_pow_ker_eval_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/EvaluationIdeal.lean)
allows arbitrary points `a : σ → R`. Both results allow arbitrary variable
types, independent coefficient/variable universes, and every `n : ℕ`, including zero.

headlines.title: Separated polynomial point quotients are square-zero extensions
headlines.text:
**Separated polynomial point quotients are square-zero extensions.** Over
any commutative ring, including the zero ring, and any index type, the
[generator-prescribed forward map](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/PointSquareZeroPresentation.lean)
from the quotient by coordinate squares and point relations is bijective
when differences of distinct evaluation points are units. The resulting
[polynomial-algebra equivalence](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/PointSquareZeroQuotient.lean)
has forward coordinate laws and an inverse law on the evaluation summands;
no mixed-product relations are added to the defining ideal. See the
[API guide](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/docs/API.md) for the two modules and their boundary examples.

headlines.title: Subset-weight-one valuations have full rational residue fields
headlines.text:
**Subset-weight-one valuations have full rational residue fields.** For any
field, any variable type and subset containing a chosen pivot, the
[weight-one construction](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/WeightOneValuation.lean)
identifies the multivariate function field birationally with a univariate
rational function field over the field of unweighted variables and pivot
ratios. Minimum subset weight gives a surjective rank-one discrete valuation;
its pivot is a uniformizer, and its entire residue field is the rational
function field in those unweighted variables and ratios. The equal-order
fraction law computes residues from initial coefficients. For the empty
subset, the separate trivial valuation has no discrete-valuation claim.

headlines.title: Hilbert basis theorem for left-Noetherian rings
headlines.text:
**Hilbert basis theorem for left-Noetherian rings.**
[`Polynomial.isNoetherianRing_of_isNoetherianRing`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/Noetherian.lean)
proves `IsNoetherianRing (Polynomial R)` for any `R : Type u` with
`[Ring R]` and `[IsNoetherianRing R]`. The polynomial variable is central;
coefficient commutativity, nontriviality and absence of zero divisors are
not required. On commutative rings,
`Polynomial.isNoetherianRing_of_isNoetherianRing_eq_isNoetherianRing`
identifies this proof with Mathlib's `Polynomial.isNoetherianRing`.
For any finite type `σ : Type v`, the named theorem
`AddMonoidAlgebra.isNoetherianRing_finsupp` proves left Noetherianity of
`AddMonoidAlgebra R (σ →₀ ℕ)`, with independently polymorphic universes.
It permits zero and noncommutative coefficient rings. For commutative rings,
this is definitionally `MvPolynomial σ R`.
Here `IsNoetherianRing R` means `IsNoetherian R R` for the canonical left
self-action. It does not assume `IsNoetherian R (Polynomial R)`: that
coefficient-module property is false for every nontrivial coefficient ring.
The [examples](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomialsTests/Noetherian.lean) include the
noncommutative 16-element ring `Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) (ZMod 2)`, whose
polynomial ring is infinite but left-Noetherian, the zero ring `ZMod 1`,
and `ZMod 4` with its nonzero nilpotent `2`.

headlines.title: Noetherian polynomial-ring criteria
headlines.text:
**Noetherian polynomial-ring criteria.** The
[Noetherian module](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/Noetherian.lean) proves the
coefficient-and-variable characterization over arbitrary commutative rings:
`MvPolynomial σ R` is Noetherian for its self-action exactly when `R` is
Noetherian and either
`σ` is finite or `R` is the zero ring. For nontrivial commutative semirings,
Noetherianity of the polynomial semiring forces `σ` to be finite; no
semiring Hilbert-basis sufficiency is asserted. The nontrivial-ring form
removes the zero-ring alternative without imposing a domain hypothesis.
The coefficient and variable universes are independent. The
[examples](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomialsTests/Noetherian.lean) distinguish empty,
finite and infinite variables over the integers, `ZMod 6`, and `ZMod 1`.

headlines.title: Artinian polynomial-semiring criteria
headlines.text:
**Artinian polynomial-semiring criteria.** For any `R : Type u` with
`[Semiring R]`, including noncommutative coefficients,
[`Polynomial.isArtinianRing_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/Artinian.lean)
proves `IsArtinianRing (Polynomial R) ↔ Subsingleton R`.
For arbitrary variable types `σ : Type u` and coefficients `R : Type v`
with `[CommSemiring R]`,
[`MvPolynomial.isArtinianRing_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/Artinian.lean)
proves `IsArtinianRing (MvPolynomial σ R) ↔ IsArtinianRing R ∧
(IsEmpty σ ∨ Subsingleton R)`. Both use polynomial multiplication on the
canonical left self-module, not the coefficient `R`-module action.
All universes are arbitrary; the multivariate universes are independent.
No ring or finite-variable hypothesis is imposed. Empty multivariate
variables recover coefficient Artinianity; trivial coefficients make every
polynomial zero. The [univariate applications](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomialsTests/PolynomialArtinianClient.lean)
include the usual non-ring semiring `ℝ≥0`, the noncommutative 16-element
matrix ring over `ZMod 2`, and the zero ring `ZMod 1`.

headlines.title: Univariate coefficient-module Noetherianity and Artinianity each characterize trivial coefficients
headlines.text:
**Univariate coefficient-module Noetherianity and Artinianity each characterize trivial coefficients.**
For any `R : Type u` with `[Semiring R]`,
[`Polynomial.isNoetherian_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/Noetherian.lean) and
[`Polynomial.isArtinian_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/Artinian.lean) give
`IsNoetherian R (Polynomial R) ↔ Subsingleton R` and
`IsArtinian R (Polynomial R) ↔ Subsingleton R`, respectively.
Both use the canonical left coefficient action
`r • p = Polynomial.C r * p`, not polynomial multiplication as a self-module.
The universe is arbitrary; no commutativity, ring, domain or field hypothesis
is required. The [coefficient-module examples](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomialsTests/PolynomialCoefficientModules.lean)
distinguish these properties from coefficient self-Noetherianity and
self-Artinianity, even for the infinite non-ring semiring `ℝ≥0` with finitely
many ideals.

headlines.title: Radical coefficient-ideal extensions are characterized by subtractivity
headlines.text:
**Radical coefficient-ideal extensions are characterized by subtractivity.**
For any commutative semiring `R`, ideal `I`, and nonempty variable type `σ`,
[`MvPolynomial.isRadical_map_C_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/CoefficientIdealSubtractive.lean)
says that `I.map C` is radical exactly when `I` is radical and satisfies
`a ∈ I → a + b ∈ I → b ∈ I`. The
[sufficiency theorem](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/CoefficientIdealSubtractive.lean)
also allows empty variable types. The coefficient and variable universes are
independent; no properness, ring, domain, reducedness or finiteness hypothesis
is needed. The [examples](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomialsTests/CoefficientIdealSubtractive.lean)
include the proper nonzero kernel of reduction `ℕ →+* ZMod 2` and the
original prime-extension and radical-extension necessity applications.

headlines.title: Coefficient-and-variable ideals have an exact finite-generation criterion
headlines.text:
**Coefficient-and-variable ideals have an exact finite-generation criterion.**
For any commutative semiring `R`, coefficient ideal `I`, and variable subset `S`,
[`MvPolynomial.ideal_map_C_sup_span_X_image_fg_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/IdealOfVars.lean)
characterizes finite generation of `Ideal.map C I ⊔ Ideal.span (X '' S)`:
`I` must be finitely generated, and either `S` is finite or `I` is the unit ideal.
The coefficient and variable universes are independent; no ring, domain,
subtractivity or finite-ambient-variable hypothesis is required. The
[examples](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomialsTests/CoefficientVariableIdeal.lean) include
a proper nonsubtractive ideal over `ℕ`, coefficient zero divisors, and the
zero-ring boundary.

headlines.title: The variable ideal is not finitely generated
headlines.text:
**The variable ideal is not finitely generated.** For a nontrivial
commutative semiring and infinitely many variables,
[`MvPolynomial.idealOfVars_not_fg`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/IdealOfVars.lean)
proves non-finite generation. A finite union of polynomial supports misses
some variable; evaluation separating that variable gives a contradiction.
Mathlib supplies the complementary *finite*-variable ideal theorem. This
library does not prove the motivating complete short exact sequence.

headlines.title: Antichain coefficients of monomial ideals
headlines.text:
**Antichain coefficients of monomial ideals.** For any commutative semiring
`R`, arbitrary variable type `σ` and antichain `S : Set (σ →₀ ℕ)`,
[`MvPolynomial.monomialIdealCoeffMap`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/MonomialIdeal.lean)
restricts coefficients from the stock ideal generated by the monic monomials
with exponents in `S` to `S →₀ R`. It is surjective and semilinear over
`constantCoeff`, for the full polynomial-semiring action on the ideal and
the coefficient action on the target. Its coordinate and monomial laws give
the original coefficients and the corresponding single functions.
Coefficients and variables have independent universes; empty or infinite
antichains and variable types, and trivial coefficients, are allowed. The
[coordinate-axes example](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomialsTests/MonomialIdealGenerators.lean)
records the three exponents of `(xy, xz, yz)` over `ℂ`, their antichain and
monomial presentation, and the ideal's nonzeroness and properness.
For **finite** `S` and **nontrivial** `R`,
[`MvPolynomial.spanFinrank_ideal_span_monomial`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/MonomialIdeal.lean)
proves that the ideal's minimum number of polynomial generators is `S.ncard`.
[`MvPolynomial.card_le_card_of_span_eq_ideal_span_monomial`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/MonomialIdeal.lean)
bounds every finite generating set, not only sets of monomials. This is
generation over the full polynomial semiring, not coefficient-module dimension.
The coordinate-axes example consequently has minimum number of generators three.

headlines.title: Variable classes form the augmentation cotangent basis
headlines.text:
**Variable classes form the augmentation cotangent basis.** For any
`(σ : Type u)` and `(R : Type v) [CommRing R]`,
[`MvPolynomial.idealOfVarsCotangentBasis`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/Cotangent.lean)
is a `σ`-indexed `R`-basis of the stock variable-ideal cotangent `I/I²`.
Its vectors are the classes of `X i`, with inherited coefficient action
`r • [p] = [C r * p]`. The `_apply` and `_repr_X` lemmas characterize those
vectors, and `idealOfVarsCotangentBasis_repr_toCotangent` computes each
coordinate as `(x : MvPolynomial σ R).coeff (Finsupp.single i 1)` for any
representative `x` in the variable ideal. Quadratic and higher terms do not
contribute. The variable and coefficient universes are independent; empty
or infinite variable types, zero rings and nilpotent coefficients are allowed.
This is an indexed basis, not a numerical rank assertion over the zero ring.

headlines.title: Degree-controlled finite interpolation
headlines.text:
**Degree-controlled finite interpolation.** Over any commutative ring `R`,
let `s : Finset ι` select points `a : ι → σ → R`. If, for every distinct
`i, j ∈ s`, the coordinate differences `a i x - a j x` span the unit ideal,
then any prescribed values `v : ι → R` are attained on `s` by a polynomial
of total degree at most `s.card - 1`
([`MvPolynomial.exists_eval_eq_totalDegree_le_of_pairwise_span_eq_top`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/Interpolation.lean)).
Both the variable type and ambient label type may be infinite; no field or
domain hypothesis is needed. The theorem asserts existence, not uniqueness.

headlines.title: Comparison with Lagrange interpolation
headlines.text:
**Comparison with Lagrange interpolation.** Over a field, for a unique
variable type, a polynomial taking prescribed values at distinct nodes and
having total degree strictly below the number of nodes maps to Mathlib's
Lagrange interpolant under the canonical single-variable equivalence
([`MvPolynomial.uniqueAlgEquiv_eq_interpolate_of_eval_eq`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/MultivariatePolynomials/LagrangeComparison.lean)).
The univariate degree bound follows from the total-degree bound. On a
nonempty selection, the bound `s.card - 1` also suffices, so the comparison
applies to any bounded witness supplied by the commutative-ring existence
theorem. Zero agrees with the empty interpolant separately; an arbitrary
degree-zero witness need not do so.

The [full results guide](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/docs/Results.md) also covers simultaneous finite-fraction
origins and their preimage dimension bounds, polynomial Zariski topology,
valuation naturality, evaluation kernels, coefficient-module Noetherianity and
Artinianity, polynomial self-Artinianity, and the substitution, degree, division
and lifting interfaces, with all their hypotheses and boundary cases.
Its [fraction examples](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/multivariate-polynomials/blob/724d9804aa6e853d9fe34f6a35c5c0d35c7f8c6a/docs/Results.md#fraction-origins-and-traces-in-use)
explain how to use the common finite stage and why whole stage fields do not
provide the subsemiring dimension bound.
